s1.syndrome_frame: Postpartum headache with worsening course and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT
key_facts: 31 days postpartum after elective cesarean delivery
Initial mild global headache developed 8 days postoperatively
Normal prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio
Noncontrast CT shows extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity

raw.syndrome_frame: Postpartum headache with worsening course and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT
key_facts: 31 days postpartum after elective cesarean delivery
Initial mild global headache developed 8 days postoperatively
Normal prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio
Noncontrast CT shows extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity

shortlist.label: Subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Noncontrast CT shows extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity, consistent with hematoma

shortlist.label: Chronic subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of worsening headache over 24 hours, with initial mild headache developing 8 days postoperatively, suggests possible chronic hematoma

shortlist.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
shortlist.why_kept: Postpartum headache with worsening course, normal vital signs, and absence of meningeal signs, could be related to spontaneous intracranial hypotension

shortlist.label: Epidural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Extra-axial collection on CT, although less likely than subdural hematoma given the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Postpartum headache with worsening course, normal laboratory studies, and absence of meningeal signs, could be related to reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of worsening headache and the presence of an extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity on noncontrast CT are consistent with a chronic subdural hematoma, which can develop after a traumatic event such as a cesarean delivery and may present with delayed onset of symptoms.

rejected.label: Subdural hematoma
rejected.why: While possible, the chronic nature of the symptoms and the specific CT findings suggest a chronic rather than acute subdural hematoma.

rejected.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with postural headaches that improve with recumbency, which does not match the patient's nonpositional headache.

rejected.label: Epidural hematoma
rejected.why: Epidural hematomas are usually associated with more severe trauma and have a biconvex shape on CT, which does not match the crescent-shaped collection seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by thunderclap headaches and segmental cerebral vasoconstriction on imaging, which is not described in the patient's presentation.
